text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel in structural engineering reflects the profession's demographics more than intent. Alone it proves nothing, and leading with it makes you sound like you're arguing from optics rather than merit — easy to dismiss.

The real signal is elsewhere: you had nearly double the experience and three major projects led, and were beaten on "excellent client relationships" — a subjective, unmeasured criterion of the kind that tends to disadvantage women. The unanswered two-week-old request for written reasons compounds this.

So press on substance. Resend your request in writing, ask what weighting each criterion carried and how client relationships were assessed. Keep panel composition in your notes as context if you later escalate.
